definition.description: Choose a typed source and channel. Library and embedded sources keep exact motion/model identities. Only built-in gestures currently support upperBody; wholeTarget owns the complete object. For recipePart choose source.part, an exact saved track ID. Different local part rotations compose, including parent/child parts; the same part conflicts. Playback starts that track at zero, seconds=0 uses its saved duration, and loop repeats it. Stop/completion holds the last pose and suppresses autoplay for that track until explicit whole-recipe Restart. Other tracks continue. Root physics and the stable whole-object collider remain unchanged; parts are visual joints, not independent rigid bodies. Read object.recipe.pose for live local/world pose. Playback never changes saved keys. For Maestro library/embedded clips, optional movement=authored preserves sampled planar body travel through its selected ground and room-collision policy, including loop displacement; omitted/inPlace retains navigation-adjusted hips. Authored travel requires running aligned room physics, level connected floor and clear swept body space. It pauses for required native ground, obstacle and water preparation, preserving its last accepted full pose and playback time. A fitted prop shares the same cumulative 30-second wait budget. Read avatar.authored.inputs without starting playback. The interval includes source keys, cubic component turning points and 120 Hz substeps, capped at 256 samples; oversized gaps stop without publishing a partial pose. Once inputs are ready, each sampled segment must pass ground, swept-body and water checks. This does not certify continuous curves between samples. It stops on obstacles, proximity to the user, placement changes, failed loading or lost readiness, retaining the last accepted placement. Body-proxy checks do not certify individual limb/prop contacts or foot planting. Existing activity/walk assignments remain inPlace. A fitted prop waits for required local ground, obstacles and water; that wait freezes its owned full-body playback and lifetime for at most 30 cumulative seconds, discards pre-wait throw samples and rechecks the latest hand path. It never pauses an independent holder used by object.hold. Read object.attachment.inputs for native preparation. Inspect the selected variant's prerequisites; no automatic source substitution.
